source.label: FIBA Official EuroBasket Champions & History Roll

historyCoverage: Complete modern FIBA EuroBasket championship finals archive (1995–2022).

records.margin: Mercedes-Benz Arena, Berlin; Willy Hernangómez Tournament MVP; Juancho Hernangómez sank 7 three-pointers in final
Sinan Erdem Dome, Istanbul; Goran Dragić scored 35 points (MVP); 18-year-old Luka Dončić won historic gold
Stade Pierre-Mauroy, Lille; Pau Gasol Tournament MVP after 40-point semi-final against France in front of 27,000 fans
Arena Stožice, Ljubljana; Tony Parker Tournament MVP (guided France to maiden EuroBasket title)
Žalgiris Arena, Kaunas; Juan Carlos Navarro Tournament MVP (27 pts in final); back-to-back European crowns
Spodek, Katowice; Pau Gasol Tournament MVP (first EuroBasket gold in Spanish basketball history)
Palacio de Deportes, Madrid; J.R. Holden stole ball and sank game-winner with 2.1s left to stun hosts Spain
Belgrade Arena; Theodoros Papaloukas (22 pts); Dirk Nowitzki named Tournament MVP
Globe Arena, Stockholm; Šarūnas Jasikevičius Tournament MVP; Lithuania went undefeated 6-0
Abdi İpekçi Arena, Istanbul; Peja Stojaković Tournament MVP; Svetislav Pešić coach
Palais Omnisports de Paris-Bercy; Gregor Fučka Tournament MVP; Carlton Myers led Azzurri to 2nd European gold
Palau Sant Jordi, Barcelona; Sasha Djordjević Tournament MVP; defended European title
O.A.C.A., Athens; Sasha Djordjević erupted for 41 points (9/12 threes); Arvydas Sabonis scored 20 pts
